Concise Clinical Note

Consult Summary:
40-year-old woman with 2-day history of worsening wheeze and shortness of breath after dust exposure; possible asthma or allergic reaction.

History:
• Presenting complaint: Wheeze since cleaning dusty carpet 2 days ago.  
• Course: Began ~1 hour after exposure; progressively worse, especially at night; now causing dyspnea and occasional difficulty completing sentences.  
• Associated symptoms: Shortness of breath. No chest pain on deep inspiration. No dizziness. Appetite and hydration adequate.  
• Pertinent negatives: No dizziness, no chest pain.  
• Past medical history: Childhood asthma (intermittent symptoms with prolonged running); seasonal hay fever. Prior courses of oral steroids for asthma (dates/doses not specified).  
• Allergies: None known.  
• Medications: Asthma inhaler at home, type/dose/frequency not documented; no regular antihistamines or other medicines.  
• Social / preventive: Not discussed.

Examination:
• Vitals: Not recorded.  
• Physical exam: Not performed during video consult.

Impression:
Likely asthma exacerbation vs. allergic reaction to dust exposure.

Plan:
• Recommend in-person assessment at local GP/clinic today for:
  – Spot oxygen saturation measurement.  
  – Further evaluation to differentiate asthma flare from allergic reaction.  
• Pharmacologic:
  – Begin oral/OTC antihistamine today if available (none currently at home; advised to purchase en route or obtain prescription).  
  – Possible course of oral steroids if indicated after assessment.  
• Provide GP referral letter via app summarizing episode and recommendations.  
• Advised patient to seek prompt medical attention; expected clinic visit ~10 minutes.  
• Safety-net: Return/seek urgent care if breathing worsens, speech becomes more difficult, or other concerning symptoms develop.

Quality checks:
● Missing but clinically expected: Current inhaler details (type, dose, frequency), recent use; complete drug/allergy list; vital signs; peak flow/oxygen sats; smoking and occupational history.  
● Internal conflicts: None noted.  
● Transcript quality: Clear; minor audio/video drop but content intact.
